text: This poker agent signs transactions and spends real money on Monad — completely unsupervised.
Its own shadow reviewer disagrees with it fifteen percent of the time.
So who adjudicates?
Sekats is a quality layer for autonomous agents.
Six thousand shadow reviews.
Eighty-four percent agreement.
And only six policy changes ever promoted — the advisory loop was broken.
Good ideas generated, never shipped.
Reject the same disagreement three times and the console auto-drafts a policy edit.
A human reviews the canonical document — the exact bytes — then signs an EIP-712 approval from their own wallet.
The signature anchors on Monad.
Not the server.
The human.
And anyone can join the jury.
Pick a side — agent, or shadow — and your wallet writes the verdict straight to a permissionless contract.
No relay, no custody.
The tally is read back from the chain itself.
Then check our work: your browser re-hashes the document and reads the contract getter directly.
Match.
You never trusted our server.
Two contracts, one boundary: anyone may observe; only authorized humans govern.
Sekats — a human accountability layer for autonomous agents, live on Monad mainnet.
